faqs.q: There are bats in my Pomaria attic. When can they be removed?
faqs.a: Bats are excluded, never trapped or killed, and South Carolina requires no permit to remove them. Timing follows SCDNR guidance rather than a state ban: complete exclusions are scheduled for early spring (March–April) or late summer into fall (August–October), because excluding in May through mid-July can trap flightless pups inside. In Pomaria we fit one-way exits over the entry points used by colonies near Broad River-side farm country in the county's east, seal every other gap of 3/8 inch or more, and clean guano once the colony is out. A single bat found in living quarters is different — do not handle it, and it should go to the SC Department of Public Health for rabies testing.

faqs.q: Are armadillos really established around Pomaria?
faqs.a: Yes — nine-banded armadillos are established throughout the entirety of South Carolina, and Pomaria is no exception. They root up lawns hunting grubs and worms and dig burrows under porches, driveways, and crawlspace edges near Broad River-side farm country in the county's east. We trap the animals working your property and then backfill and screen the burrow openings, because an open burrow is quickly claimed by the next armadillo — or by a skunk or opossum. Routine relocation is not permitted in South Carolina, so removal follows SCDNR depredation rules.

faqs.q: What does a wildlife removal job in Pomaria actually involve?
faqs.a: It starts with the inspection, and the scope grows or shrinks with what that inspection finds around Broad River-side farm country in the county's east: how many entry points the animal has opened, whether young are present, and how much exclusion the roofline and crawlspace need. A single squirrel entry sealed in a day is a small job; a raccoon family with latrine cleanup and a full roofline seal is a larger one. We walk you through each item we find before the work is set, so the scope you approve is the scope we do.
